mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential downturn.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained decline, or if the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase, or if the correlation between HOUST increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where GDPC1 shows a sustained decline, or if the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
